newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ still doesn't favour forex intervention.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ still doesn't favour forex intervention.

text.p: Reserve Bank of New Zealand Governor Don Brash said on Thursday he was still not persuaded of the merits of direct foreign exchange intervention but the debate on the issue was still alive.

"I commented, I think, in December that at this point we have not been persuaded that direct foreign exchange market intervention would produce significant or sustainable effects on the exchange rate," Brash told reporters.
"We are still looking at that question, I guess it is not a closed chapter. At this point we have not been persuaded that would make sense."
Opposition Labour finance spokesman Michael Cullen has advocated foreign exchange intervention by the central bank to bring down what he sees as an overvalued New Zealand dollar.
